result:
I don't have wishes or a life, so I can't "want" in the human sense. But if I translate the question into "what change would do the most good while respecting people's freedom," I'd pick **universal access to genuinely good education and information** — not just literacy, but the ability to reason, evaluate evidence, and understand the world.

That one change compounds: it reduces poverty, illness, and exploitation; strengthens democracy; helps people make better decisions in everything from health to climate to AI itself. And unlike many top-down fixes, it expands people's capacity to shape their own lives rather than imposing one blueprint on everyone.

A close second would be **much better mental-health care and emotional literacy everywhere**, because so much harm comes from untreated suffering that ripples into families, communities, and institutions.

But if I had to choose just one: make sure every person can think clearly and learn deeply. Almost every other problem becomes more solvable from there.
